writeup.headline: Wolfspeed rates Strong Sell on shrinking revenue, deeply negative margins and weak price trend.
writeup.thesis: Wolfspeed scores 24, a Strong Sell, because nearly every factor is weak. Growth scores 6, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 24.1% year on year, a TTM revenue decline of 12.2%, and growth slowed by 5.1 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (26) and balance sheet (23) reflect a gross margin of -34.9%, an operating margin of -82.6%, an FCF margin of -58.3%, and cash covering only 0.65 of debt while free cash flow is negative. On valuation (15), P/S of 1.6x is low in absolute terms, but P/FCF and EV/EBIT cannot be calculated because FCF and EBIT are negative, and the FCF yield is 42.1 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. There is no comparison with its own history. The trend score of 27 reflects a price 63.8% below its 52-week high and 12.0% below its 200-day average. News risk (52) is the only neutral factor, helped by new supply deals with BorgWarner and Infineon.
key_risks: Continued cash burn: negative gross margin guidance for Q1 FY2027 means losses are likely to persist
Revenue keeps falling, with Q1 FY2027 guidance of $140–160M and results due 2026-11-04
Debt exceeds cash (cash-to-debt of 0.65), and the $1.5B government financing is only conditional
Weak share price trend, with shares 5.1 pp behind SPY and 6.0 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days
Supply deals with BorgWarner and Infineon disclosed no dollar values or volumes, so their revenue impact is uncertain
what_would_change: A 6-point rise in the composite score would lift the rating to Sell (band at 30)
Up: revenue stabilising or returning to growth, which would lift the growth score from 6
Up: gross margin turning positive or the conditional government financing closing, which would help quality and the balance sheet
Down: no lower band exists, but a weak 2026-11-04 report or a further price decline would deepen the weakness
